details: Bitcoin traded around $59,940 on Sunday, putting it on track for a rare second consecutive quarterly loss after falling below $60,000. Major altcoins like Ether, Dogecoin, and XRP experienced significant weekly declines. Market sentiment is characterized by "Extreme Fear," driven by continued outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs and a hawkish Federal Reserve outlook, with BTC losing nearly 20% in June and over 30% year-to-date.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $60K Amid Bearish Market & ETF Outflows

details: Bitcoin advocate Samson Mow asserts that the current Bitcoin market has hit its bottom, arguing that institutional inflows from spot ETFs have accelerated and fundamentally altered the traditional four-year halving cycle. However, other analysts remain cautious, with some predicting further price drops to $40,000-$55,000 later this year based on technical indicators like bear crosses in moving averages.
title: Samson Mow Claims Bitcoin Bottom Amid Analyst Skepticism

details: Michael Saylor, Executive Chairman of Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy), has hinted at further Bitcoin purchases, consistent with his pattern of social media teasers preceding official announcements. This comes as MicroStrategy's substantial Bitcoin holdings face approximately $13 billion in unrealized losses, raising questions about its financing model and dividend coverage. Saylor has consistently reiterated his long-term conviction in Bitcoin.
title: Michael Saylor Hints at More Bitcoin Buys Despite MicroStrategy Losses

details: SecondFi, a Cardano-based wallet, is targeting a two-week timeline to begin returning 16 million ADA (valued at approximately $2.4 million) stolen from 374 wallets in a June 23 exploit. The vulnerability was found in the wallet's web generation software, which exposed private keys. Users are advised to await official instructions and beware of fraudulent recovery attempts.
title: SecondFi Plans Two-Week Recovery After Cardano Wallet Exploit

details: A Reuters poll reveals that economists now largely anticipate no Federal Reserve interest rate cuts until 2028, a drastic shift from previous forecasts predicting a cut in 2026. This hawkish repricing of expectations follows the Fed's recent FOMC meeting and signals a prolonged period of tighter monetary conditions, which typically weighs negatively on risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Economists Push Fed Rate Cut Expectations to 2028

details: The average investor in BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) is now down approximately 40%, a stark reversal from a 30% gain in mid-2025. This reflects the impact of Bitcoin's recent price declines and substantial outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs, totaling around $5 billion this year. This "brutal intro to BTC" has impacted many mainstream investors.
title: BlackRock IBIT Investors Face 40% Loss Amid Bitcoin Drop

details: Cathie Wood's Ark Invest has increased its exposure to crypto-linked equities, purchasing shares in Coinbase (COIN), Circle (CRCL), and Bullish (BLSH) across several ETFs. The firm spent approximately $2.1 million on these positions, resuming its accumulation after a week-long pause and amidst a broader selloff in the crypto stock market. This indicates continued confidence in the long-term prospects of these companies.
title: Ark Invest Buys Crypto Stocks Amid Market Pullback

details: Standard Chartered's Head of Digital Assets Research has reportedly projected that the Aave (AAVE) token, a prominent decentralized finance (DeFi) lending platform, could reach $3,500 by 2030. This optimistic forecast is based on the bank's expectation that the broader DeFi market could expand to an estimated $2.7 trillion within the same timeframe, highlighting the growing institutional interest in decentralized lending protocols.
title: Standard Chartered Predicts Aave (AAVE) to Reach $3,500 by 2030
